requirements.req_text: Do the following: (a) Explain to your counselor the most likely hazards you may encounter while participating in geocaching activities, and what you should do to anticipate, help prevent, mitigate, and respond to these hazards. (b) Discuss first aid and prevention for the types of injuries or illnesses that could occur while participating in geocaching activities, including cuts, scrapes, snakebite, insect stings, tick bites, exposure to poisonous plants, heat and cold reactions (sunburn, heatstroke, heat exhaustion, hypothermia), and dehydration. (c) Discuss how to properly plan an activity that uses GPS, including using the buddy system, sharing your plan with others, and considering the weather, route, and proper attire.

pamphlet_excerpts: Identifying Poisonous Local Plants: Learn how to recognize, and avoid, the poisonous plants in your area, such as poison ivy, poison oak, and poison sumac (p. 66).
Immediate Soap and Water Wash: If you think you have touched a poisonous plant, immediately wash the affected skin with soap and water (p. 66).
Alcohol and Calamine Skin Care: Wipe with rubbing alcohol and apply a soothing skin treatment such as calamine lotion (p. 66).
Protective Clothing Against Sunburn: Prevent sunburn by limiting exposure to the sun, covering up, and wearing a broad-brimmed hat (p. 66).
step_by_step_procedure: Step 1 - Apply Alcohol and Calamine Lotion: Wipe with rubbing alcohol and apply a soothing skin treatment such as calamine lotion (p. 66).
Step 2 - Wear Broad Brimmed Sun Hats: Prevent sunburn by limiting exposure to the sun, covering up, and wearing a broad-brimmed hat (p. 66).
Step 3 - Apply Minimum SPF 15 Sunscreen: Use a sunscreen with a sun protection factor (SPF) of at least 15 (p. 66).
Step 4 - Cool Sunburns With Wet Cloths: Treat a painful sunburn by applying cool, wet cloths (p. 66).

Respecting Historic Structures and Artifacts: Observe, but do not touch, cultural or historic structures and artifacts (p. 54).
Protecting Artifacts From Cache Use: Never use artifacts as cache items (p. 54).
step_by_step_procedure: Step 1 - Leave Historic Structures Untouched: Observe, but do not touch, cultural or historic structures and artifacts (p. 54).
Step 2 - Exclude Artifacts From Cache Containers: Never use artifacts as cache items (p. 54).
Step 3 - Replace Lifted Rocks Carefully: If you lift a rock to look under it, replace it exactly as you found (p. 54).
Step 4 - Preserve Natural Settings Intact: Never destroy any natural setting, whether you are hiding or seeking a geocache (p. 54).

pamphlet_excerpts: Continuous Global Satellite Coverage: GPS technology can be used anywhere in the world 24 hours a day because the system of satellites circles Earth all the time, and some number of them (p. 11).
All Weather Free Operation: The system works in any kind of weather and does not require any setup fee or subscription charge (p. 11).
Timing Orbiting Satellite Signals: A GPS receiver (GPSr) calculates its position by carefully timing the signals sent by the 24 to 30 GPS satellites high above Earth (p. 11).
Multiple Satellites Overhead Everywhere: At any given time, there are usually several satellites over any given place on Earth (p. 11).
step_by_step_procedure: Step 1 - Calculate Position From Signals: A GPS receiver (GPSr) calculates its position by carefully timing the signals sent by the 24 to 30 GPS satellites high above Earth (p. 11).
Step 2 - Track Multiple Overhead Satellites: At any given time, there are usually several satellites over any given place on Earth (p. 11).
Step 3 - Receive Satellite Time Data: Each satellite continually transmits data that indicates its location and the current time (p. 11).
Step 4 - Compare Signal Arrival Times: All GPS satellites transmit signals at the same instant, but the signals arrive at a GPS receiver at slightly different times (p. 11).

patrol_quiz_bank.explanation: Correct Answer (D): All GPS satellites transmit their location and current time simultaneously, and the receiver calculates its position by measuring the slight differences in arrival times from 24 to 30 orbiting satellites (p. 11).
